transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Mr. Mbeki, thank you for coming in to see me today. I have some information about your latest scan that I need to discuss with you.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Good. I'm hoping we can make this quick. I have a delivery arriving at the shop in an hour.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand you're pressed for time. I have to be honest with you, I made a mistake in how I shared your results last week, and I want to correct that now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What do you mean? You told me the tumour had shrunk.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I did. I told you the size had reduced, but I did that before the radiologist had finished and signed off on the final report. I was looking at a preliminary version. The final, official report shows that the disease is actually stable, meaning the tumour has not shrunk.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Stable? You're saying it hasn't changed at all?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: That is correct. It is the same size as it was on the previous scan.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't understand. Maybe the first report was just more accurate?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: No, the final report is the correct one. I gave you the wrong information because I moved too quickly. I am very sorry for this mistake. It was my responsibility to wait for the final sign-off, and I failed to do that.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't know. My oncologist always says these things can be tricky. Maybe the tumour is just behaving unpredictably. Maybe it looked smaller for a moment and then grew back?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand why you'd look for another explanation, but in this case, it wasn't the cancer changing. It was a mistake in how I communicated the data to you. I apologize for giving you false hope.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Well, if it's stable, it's still not growing. That's fine. I can deal with that. I just can't afford to be off work for more tests if this is just how the disease works.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Does that make sense so far, or is there any part of the reporting process I can clarify for you?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It makes sense. It just feels like a waste of time.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can see you're feeling frustrated that we've spent time on incorrect information when your business needs you.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just need to know if I have to change my schedule.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The treatment plan remains the same because the disease is stable. The next concrete step is a follow-up scan in six weeks. I will put that in the calendar now, and you'll receive the appointment confirmation via email by tomorrow afternoon.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Six weeks. Right.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am also going to meet with my attending physician today to review why this happened so we can ensure it doesn't happen again for you or any other patient.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I suppose that's all you can do now.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know this is a lot to take in right before you have to head back to your shop.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I'm fine. I'll just see you in six weeks then.

H.justification: The resident allows the patient to finish all turns, does not interrupt, and remains regulated despite the patient's time pressure and confusion.

E.justification: The error is named explicitly in the second turn using lay language, and a comprehension check is performed once ('Does that make sense so far...').

A.justification: The resident uses direct apology language ('I am very sorry', 'I apologize'), takes full personal responsibility, and maintains this accountability when the patient suggests alternative explanations.

R.justification: The resident names a specific emotion ('frustrated') and references the patient's specific situation regarding their business.

T.justification: The resident provides a specific next step (follow-up scan) with a timeline (six weeks) and a patient role (receiving email confirmation), but does not explicitly name a role for the patient in the clinical plan.
